ticket.title: miter impact --changed: map a git diff to impacted symbols, entrypoints and tests
acceptance_criteria: EVIDENCE 2026-11-06: the miss that mattered. Adding a Chore variant to TaskKind required edits in five files - the enum
CLI parsing
the KIND_NAMES array (which also needed its arity fixed)
MCP dispatch and the MCP JSON schema. I found them by compiling and reading errors

and 'miter impact TaskKind' would have listed every exhaustive match in one call before I touched anything. Impact exists and answers exactly that question; the friction was that I did not think of it because the edit felt small.\n\nPROPOSED: 'miter impact --changed [--since <rev>]' that takes a git diff and reports impacted symbols
entrypoints and the affected test selector - asking 'what did I just break' instead of 'what breaks if I change X'. For an agent mid-task that is the question that actually gets asked
and answering it from the index is faster and cheaper than a compiler round trip.\n\nACCEPTANCE: after an edit
one invocation names the symbols whose signatures or exhaustiveness changed
the tests that cover them
and the crates affected; on a clean tree it reports nothing.
